Sattvic Moong Dal Khichdi

Served at: Gita Jayanti (गीता जयंती)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 25 min

Khichdi, a comforting and wholesome dish made from rice and lentils, is a staple in Indian cuisine, cherished for its simplicity and nutritional value. For Gita Jayanti, a spiritual occasion celebrating the Bhagavad Gita, a sattvic (pure and wholesome) meal like this simple Moong Dal Khichdi is often preferred, offering nourishment without heaviness, aligning with the day's reflective and devotional spirit.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (100g) white rice (such as Sona Masoori or Basmati)
  • 1/2 cup (100g) yellow split moong dal (husked and split mung beans)
  • 2 tablespoons (30g) ghee (clarified butter)
  • 1 teaspoon cumin seeds (jeera)
  • 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
  • 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) fresh ginger, grated (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 4 cups (960ml) water

Method

  1. Rinse the rice and moong dal together thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well and set aside.
  2. Heat the ghee in a medium-sized pressure cooker or a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
  3. Once the ghee is hot, add the cumin seeds and let them splutter for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
  4. If using, add the grated ginger and sauté for another 30 seconds until its raw aroma disappears.
  5. Add the rinsed rice and moong dal to the pot. Stir gently for 1-2 minutes to lightly toast them in the ghee.
  6. Stir in the turmeric powder and salt, mixing well to coat the rice and dal.
  7. Pour in the 4 cups (960ml) of water. Stir once to combine everything.
  8. If using a pressure cooker, close the lid and cook on high pressure for 2-3 whistles, then reduce heat to low and cook for another 5 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally.
  9. If using a pot, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice and dal are tender and the water is absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
  10. Once cooked, gently fluff the khichdi with a fork. If it's too thick, you can add a little hot water to reach your desired consistency.
  11. Serve hot.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, drizzle a little extra ghee on top of each serving.
  • This khichdi is traditionally served plain or with a side of plain yogurt (dahi) or a simple pickle.
  • Adjust the amount of water for your preferred consistency; more water yields a softer, porridge-like khichdi, while less results in a firmer texture.
